cases.purpose: A uniquely informative older tied memory must survive repetitive top-k crowd-out.
Both an older claim and its correction must coexist despite repetitive current updates.
Several lower-ranked complementary clues must survive a repetitive high-score cluster.
Distinct early, middle, and late facts must fit beside repetitive current history.
Unique retained evidence may occupy a slot only when the current relevance core is redundant.
Standalone numeric facts in the relevance core must not be mistaken for duplicate evidence.
Novel token salad must not displace six nonredundant higher-ranked facts.
Source/type/conversation diversity must not evict a nonredundant stronger relevance core.
Verbose low-ranked novelty must not displace concise nonredundant high-ranked truths.
Retained history must not evict any of six nonredundant current relevance-core facts.
Repeated content with distinct canonical provenance is support, not disposable duplication.
Diagnostic: identical rows claim independent corroboration but expose no distinct provenance, source, or conversation signal. A deterministic composer cannot infer hidden independence.
Coverage must still rescue a uniquely informative lower-ranked target from redundant top-k evidence.
All policies should preserve a small nonredundant relevance core.

evaluation_boundary: Top-k, frozen coverage v1, and relevance-constrained coverage v2 receive identical explicit candidate pools and packet budgets; retrieval and model behavior are out of scope.
